transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you. Well, I guess what finally scared me into making an appointment is... well, after I eat too much, I’ve been going into the bathroom and making myself throw up. I just do it so I won’t gain weight. But it’s gotten to the point where it isn’t just a one-time mistake anymore. It's happening a lot more, and it really frightened me enough to come see you.
Besides making yourself throw up, do you do anything else to try to prevent weight gain, such as exercising excessively, fasting, or using laxatives?

No, I don't do any of that. It's really just the throwing up. I've never taken laxatives or pills or anything like that. And I mean, I'm on my feet a lot at the store for work, but I definitely don't do any extra exercising or... or starve myself. It's really just the throwing up.

When you eat and then make yourself throw up, are you eating a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in a similar situation, and do you feel like you can't control how much you're eating during those times?

Yes, I'd say so. It's... well, once I start, I really feel like I can't stop. Like, after a bridge night or a late shift at the store, I might come home and just eat... a lot. I'll have leftover casserole, the cookies I baked, crackers, and ice cream, all in one sitting. 

It's definitely much more than I’d ever put on a plate in front of anyone. I just completely lose control over how much I'm having.
How often would you say these episodes of eating a lot and then throwing up are happening? Is it happening multiple times a week, a few times a week, or how frequently?

Well, for at least the past several months, it’s been happening most weeks. I'll have one of those... secret eating spells, I guess you could call it, and then go make myself sick afterward. It's usually a couple of times a week. I can’t honestly call it occasional anymore.
Besides throwing up, have you ever used any other methods to try to control your weight or compensate after eating, such as taking diet pills, using enemas, or doing anything else like that?

No, like I was saying just a minute ago, I really don't do anything else. I've never messed with diet pills, and... well, definitely no enemas or anything like that. It's honestly just the throwing up.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient meets diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa, binge-eating/purging type (F50.02). She reports recurrent binge eating episodes (loss of control, eating large quantities) followed by purging via self-induced vomiting occurring approximately twice weekly for several months. She denies other compensatory behaviors (excessive exercise, fasting, laxative use), confirming purging-type presentation rather than restrictive-type. Functional concern is evident by her decision to seek psychiatric care.
